source_meta._title: Dropping item stacks from the player's hotbar in any creative inventory tab other than "Survival Inventory" deletes items

stor.recommended_version: Minecraft Java Edition 1.21 (an affected release; do not use fix version 24w33a or a later version)
stor.environment: Vanilla Minecraft Java Edition 1.21 in a single-player Creative-mode world, using keyboard and mouse. Use the default Drop Selected Item binding of Q, or confirm before testing that the action is bound to Q. No particular seed, coordinates, difficulty, or world type are required.
preconditions: Launch the game using an installation explicitly configured for Minecraft Java Edition 1.21.
Use a Creative-mode player in a loaded world.
Ensure the Drop Selected Item control is bound to Q; with default controls, this is already the case.
Have at least one empty hotbar slot. The hotbar is the row of nine item slots at the bottom of the screen and remains visible along the bottom of the Creative inventory.
Keep the Creative inventory open during the eventual drop action; do not perform the test from normal gameplay view.
Use a Creative inventory category other than Survival Inventory or Search Items. This plan uses the Combat tab.
Use a stack containing exactly one item for the deterministic reproduction path. This plan uses a Diamond Sword because it cannot stack above one item.

steps.action: From the title screen, select Singleplayer and create a new world with Game Mode set to Creative. Enter the world after creation completes. An existing Creative-mode world may be used instead if available.
steps.exact_input: Singleplayer -> Create New World -> Game Mode: Creative -> Create New World
steps.success_cue: The player is present in a world in Creative mode, with hearts and hunger indicators absent from the normal HUD.

steps.action: Wait for the world to become ready before manipulating the inventory.
steps.success_cue: Nearby terrain has rendered, player movement responds normally, and no world-loading screen is visible.

steps.action: Open the player's Creative inventory using the inventory control.
steps.success_cue: The Creative inventory interface is open, showing category tabs, an item grid, and the nine hotbar slots along the bottom.

steps.action: Select the Combat category by left-clicking its sword-icon tab. Do not select the Survival Inventory tab, and do not select Search Items because keyboard input there can be captured by the search field.
steps.success_cue: The Combat tab is highlighted, combat-related items are displayed, the Survival Inventory layout is not displayed, and no search text field has keyboard focus.

steps.action: Locate the Diamond Sword in the Combat item grid and left-click it once to pick up a copy onto the mouse cursor.
steps.success_cue: A Diamond Sword is attached to the mouse cursor. Because the item is unstackable, the held stack contains exactly one item.

steps.action: Move the cursor to an empty slot in the nine-slot hotbar at the bottom of the open inventory and left-click that slot to place the Diamond Sword there.
steps.success_cue: Exactly one Diamond Sword is present in the chosen hotbar slot, no second item is stacked with it, and the mouse cursor is no longer carrying the sword.

steps.action: Confirm that the Combat tab remains selected. If another tab was selected accidentally, select Combat again without removing the Diamond Sword from the hotbar.
steps.success_cue: The Creative inventory is still open on the Combat tab, not Survival Inventory or Search Items, and the single Diamond Sword remains in the hotbar.

steps.action: Move the mouse pointer directly over the hotbar slot containing the single Diamond Sword. Do not click the slot, close the inventory, or move the sword onto the cursor.
steps.success_cue: The pointer is hovering over the Diamond Sword's hotbar slot while the Combat tab remains open, and the slot still contains exactly one sword.

steps.action: While continuing to hover over the Diamond Sword's hotbar slot, press the Drop Selected Item key once. With the required/default binding, press Q without Ctrl. This is the single-item variant from the report.
steps.success_cue: The Q input has been issued once while the pointer was over the one-item hotbar stack and the non-Survival Creative inventory tab remained open.

stor.handoff_condition: The player has just pressed Q once while hovering over a hotbar stack containing exactly one Diamond Sword, with the Creative inventory still open on the Combat tab. Begin observation immediately without closing the inventory or performing another input.

source_meta._title: Frogspawn is not grouped with turtle eggs in the Creative inventory

stor.recommended_version: Minecraft: Java Edition 1.19 (an affected release version explicitly confirmed in the report)
stor.environment: Vanilla Minecraft: Java Edition 1.19 in a local single-player world, using Creative mode and the standard keyboard-and-mouse Creative inventory interface. Any world seed and default world-generation settings may be used.
preconditions: Minecraft: Java Edition 1.19 is installed and selectable in the Minecraft Launcher.
Use an unmodified client so that mods or datapacks do not add, remove, or reorder Creative inventory entries.
A keyboard and mouse are available. The instructions use the default Inventory key, E; if controls are rebound, use the key assigned to Inventory instead.
No particular world seed, biome, coordinates, difficulty, items, entities, or structures are required.

steps.action: In the Minecraft Launcher, select and launch the Java Edition 1.19 release profile. Do not create the test world in another Minecraft version.
steps.success_cue: The Minecraft 1.19 main menu is displayed, with the version identified as 1.19.

steps.action: Open the local world-selection screen from the main menu.
steps.success_cue: The Select World screen is displayed.

steps.action: Start creating a new test world.
steps.success_cue: The Create New World configuration screen is displayed.

steps.action: Set the new world's game mode to Creative. Click the Game Mode control until it reads "Game Mode: Creative"; leave the seed and other settings at their defaults.
steps.exact_input: Left-click the "Game Mode" control until it displays "Game Mode: Creative"
steps.success_cue: The world-creation screen explicitly displays "Game Mode: Creative".

steps.action: Create the world, then wait until world generation and initial chunk loading finish. Do not continue while a loading screen is visible.
steps.success_cue: The player can move normally in the generated world and the Creative-mode hotbar is visible without a loading overlay.

steps.action: Open the Creative inventory using the Inventory control.
steps.success_cue: The Creative inventory window is open and shows category tabs around an item grid.

steps.action: Locate the Creative inventory category named "Miscellaneous". Move the pointer over the category tabs until the hover tooltip reads "Miscellaneous"; do not use the Search Items tab because the test concerns ordering inside the Miscellaneous category.
steps.exact_input: Move the mouse pointer over Creative inventory tabs until the tooltip says "Miscellaneous"
steps.success_cue: The pointer is over a tab whose tooltip explicitly reads "Miscellaneous".

steps.action: Open the Miscellaneous category by left-clicking the tab identified in the previous step. Allow the item grid to finish displaying before any inspection or scrolling begins.
steps.success_cue: The Miscellaneous tab is selected and its item grid is visible and responsive, ready to be examined from its current position through the full list.

stor.handoff_condition: The Minecraft 1.19 Creative inventory is open with the Miscellaneous tab selected and its item grid fully displayed. Hand control to the observation subsystem so it can traverse the tab and inspect the relative inventory ordering of the turtle egg and frogspawn entries without changing categories or using Search Items.
uncertainties: The report does not specify whether the original reproduction used single-player or multiplayer. A local single-player Creative world is selected as the simplest execution path because no server-specific condition is stated.
The report does not specify a seed, coordinates, world type, difficulty, GUI scale, window size, or inventory scroll position; none is asserted as required.
The report does not identify the Miscellaneous tab by its icon, so the plan uses the tab's hover tooltip rather than assuming a potentially version-sensitive icon.
The report says to look through the Miscellaneous tab but does not prescribe a scrolling method. Scrolling and evaluating item placement are therefore left to the observation subsystem after handoff.

source_meta._title: Muddy mangrove roots are not grouped with mud in the Creative inventory

stor.recommended_version: Minecraft Java Edition 1.19.2 (latest affected full release listed in the report; do not use 22w42a or later for this reproduction)
stor.environment: Vanilla Minecraft Java Edition 1.19.2 in a single-player world with the player in Creative mode. No particular seed, location, dimension, cheats setting, or multiplayer server is required because the reproduction concerns the ordering of items in the Creative inventory.
preconditions: Install or configure a Minecraft Launcher installation for the exact Java Edition version 1.19.2.
Use an unmodified client without mods, datapacks, or resource packs that replace or reorganize the Creative inventory.
Create or load a world in which the player is in Creative mode. The simplest deterministic setup is a new single-player world created with Game Mode set to Creative.
A mouse wheel or the Creative inventory scrollbar must be available so the complete Building Blocks item list can be inspected.
Do not use the Search Items tab to locate the four items; their positions specifically within the Building Blocks tab must be preserved and inspected.

steps.action: In the Minecraft Launcher, select the installation configured for Java Edition 1.19.2 and start the game. Confirm the version shown on the title screen before continuing.
steps.success_cue: The Minecraft Java Edition title screen is open and displays version 1.19.2.

steps.action: Create a new single-player world with Game Mode set to Creative, or load an existing world where the player is already in Creative mode. A new Creative world avoids needing cheats or a game-mode command.
steps.exact_input: Singleplayer -> Create New World -> Game Mode: Creative -> Create New World
steps.success_cue: The player has entered a world and the HUD does not display Survival health and hunger bars, indicating Creative mode is active.

steps.action: Wait until the world finishes loading before opening any menus. Continue only when nearby terrain has rendered and normal player input responds without loading pauses.
steps.success_cue: Nearby chunks are visible and the player can move or look around normally.

steps.action: Open the Creative inventory using the inventory action. With default controls, press E once.
steps.success_cue: The Creative inventory interface is open, showing category tabs and a grid of obtainable items.

steps.action: Select the Building Blocks category tab. Move the pointer across the category tabs until the tooltip reads "Building Blocks", then left-click that tab. Do not switch to the Search Items tab.
steps.exact_input: Left-click the tab whose tooltip is "Building Blocks"
steps.success_cue: The Building Blocks tab is selected and its item grid is visible.

steps.action: Inspect the Building Blocks grid for Dirt. Scroll through this tab with the mouse wheel or drag its scrollbar as necessary. Hover over candidate blocks and use the tooltip to positively identify the item named "Dirt"; do not rely only on its brown texture. Record or retain its grid row, column, and approximate scrollbar position for the observation handoff.
steps.exact_input: Mouse wheel or inventory scrollbar; hover until tooltip reads "Dirt"
steps.success_cue: The tooltip "Dirt" has been displayed and the item's position within the Building Blocks list has been identified.

steps.action: Without changing Creative inventory categories, locate Rooted Dirt in the same Building Blocks item grid. Continue scrolling through the category and hover over candidate blocks until the tooltip reads "Rooted Dirt". Record or retain its grid and scrollbar position separately from Dirt.
steps.exact_input: Mouse wheel or inventory scrollbar; hover until tooltip reads "Rooted Dirt"
steps.success_cue: The tooltip "Rooted Dirt" has been displayed and the item's position within the Building Blocks list has been identified.

steps.action: Remain in the Building Blocks tab and locate Mud. Scroll through the category as needed, hover over candidate blocks, and confirm the tooltip reads "Mud". Record or retain its grid row, column, and approximate scrollbar position.
steps.exact_input: Mouse wheel or inventory scrollbar; hover until tooltip reads "Mud"
steps.success_cue: The tooltip "Mud" has been displayed and the item's position within the Building Blocks list has been identified.

steps.action: Still within the Building Blocks tab, locate Muddy Mangrove Roots. Scroll through the same category without using inventory search, hover over candidate blocks, and confirm the tooltip reads "Muddy Mangrove Roots". Record or retain its grid row, column, and approximate scrollbar position.
steps.exact_input: Mouse wheel or inventory scrollbar; hover until tooltip reads "Muddy Mangrove Roots"
steps.success_cue: The tooltip "Muddy Mangrove Roots" is visible and positions have now been identified for Dirt, Rooted Dirt, Mud, and Muddy Mangrove Roots within the Building Blocks category.

stor.handoff_condition: The Creative inventory remains open on the Building Blocks tab immediately after Muddy Mangrove Roots has been positively identified by its tooltip. The inventory positions of Dirt, Rooted Dirt, Mud, and Muddy Mangrove Roots have all been recorded or retained; hand control to the observation subsystem to compare their placement in the category.
uncertainties: The report lists four affected builds—22w14a, 1.19, 1.19.1, and 1.19.2—but does not require one specific affected build. This plan uses 1.19.2 because it is the latest affected full release explicitly confirmed in the report.
No world seed, coordinates, dimension, server configuration, or GUI scale is specified. These appear unnecessary because the tested state is the static Creative inventory ordering.

The report does not provide exact grid row, column, or scrollbar coordinates for the items. They must therefore be located by scanning the Building Blocks tab and confirming each item through its tooltip.

source_meta._title: Recipes for new waxed copper blocks are not grouped

stor.environment: A vanilla Minecraft: Java Edition 23w44a client running a local single-player world in Creative mode, with commands enabled, the Update 1.21 experiment enabled during world creation, and the game language set to English (US) so the report's literal recipe-book search text works.
preconditions: Configure the Minecraft Launcher to make snapshot installations available, then install and launch Java Edition 23w44a. Confirm that the lower-left corner of the title screen identifies the running version as 23w44a.
Use an unmodified client without additional datapacks that alter recipes or recipe-book grouping.
A new world may be used; the report does not require a particular world seed, terrain, dimension, or coordinates.
Use keyboard and mouse controls. The instructions name default controls; use the equivalent bound controls if they have been changed.

steps.action: From the 23w44a title screen, set the game language to English (US): open Options, open Language, select English (US), and confirm with Done until you return to the title screen.
steps.success_cue: The title-screen interface is displayed in English, allowing the exact recipe-book query "waxed" to match the English recipe names.

steps.action: Select Singleplayer, then select Create New World. Configure the new world to use Creative game mode and ensure commands/cheats are enabled. No particular seed is required, so leave the seed at its default random value.
steps.success_cue: The Create New World screen shows Creative as the selected game mode and commands are allowed.

steps.action: Before creating the world, open the Experiments screen from the world-creation options. Turn on the experiment labeled Update 1.21, accept the experimental-feature warning if one appears, and return to the world-creation screen without disabling the experiment.
steps.success_cue: The world-creation interface indicates that the Update 1.21 experiment is enabled.

steps.action: Select Create New World to generate and enter the experimental world.
steps.success_cue: The player appears in the world and the normal in-game HUD is visible.

steps.action: Wait until world generation and nearby chunk loading are complete. Do not continue while the loading screen is visible or while terrain is still appearing around the player.
steps.success_cue: Nearby terrain is rendered and the player can look and move normally.

steps.action: Press T to open in-game chat. Type the report's recipe command exactly as shown, including the leading slash, then press Enter to execute it as the current player.
steps.success_cue: Chat confirms that recipes were granted to the player; recipe-unlock notifications may also begin appearing.

steps.action: Press E to open the Creative inventory. Use its item search field to find a Crafting Table, then place one Crafting Table into any hotbar slot. The hotbar is the row of nine item slots shown at the bottom of the inventory and HUD.
steps.success_cue: A Crafting Table item is present in one of the nine hotbar slots.

steps.action: Close the inventory with E or Escape. Select the hotbar slot containing the Crafting Table by pressing its number key or scrolling the mouse wheel.
steps.success_cue: The Crafting Table is visibly held in the player's main hand and its hotbar slot is highlighted.

steps.action: Aim at the top surface of a nearby solid block where there is empty space above it, then right-click once to place the Crafting Table.
steps.success_cue: A Crafting Table block is visible in the world directly at the targeted placement location.

steps.action: Aim the crosshair at the placed Crafting Table and right-click once to use it.
steps.success_cue: The 3-by-3 Crafting interface is open and the placed Crafting Table remains visible behind the interface if the background is not fully obscured.

steps.action: If the recipe-book panel is not visible on the left side of the Crafting interface, click the green recipe-book button beside the crafting grid to open it. If it is already visible, leave it open.
steps.success_cue: The recipe-book panel, including its search field and recipe entries, is visible alongside the 3-by-3 crafting grid.

steps.action: In the recipe-book panel, select the general Search/All category, represented by the compass tab, so the search is not restricted to another recipe category. Also set the recipe filter to Showing All rather than Showing Craftable; hover over or click the filter button as needed to confirm its tooltip/state. This is necessary because the player is not carrying all recipe ingredients.
steps.success_cue: The compass Search/All tab is selected and the recipe-book filter reports Showing All.

steps.action: Click the recipe-book search field. Clear any existing text with Ctrl+A followed by Backspace, type the report's broad search query exactly, and leave the search results displayed without clicking or crafting a result.
steps.success_cue: The search field contains "waxed" and the recipe-book results have refreshed to entries whose English names match that search.

stor.handoff_condition: The Crafting Table interface and recipe-book panel are open, all recipes have been granted, the recipe filter is set to Showing All, and the recipe-book search has just refreshed for the query "waxed". Begin inspection of the displayed recipe entries and their grouping.
uncertainties: The report does not specify a game mode or seed. Creative mode and a fresh random-seed world are practical choices that minimize unrelated item-acquisition work and do not change the recipe-book grouping action under test.

The report lists many affected releases, but 23w44a is recommended because it matches the original experiment-based instructions and retains the original set of Update 1.21 experimental copper recipes described by the reporter.

The report also suggests the narrower searches "waxed c", "waxed e", "waxed w", and "waxed o" for isolating regular, exposed, weathered, and oxidized results. The broad query "waxed" is used as the primary deterministic trigger; the observation subsystem may substitute one of those exact narrower queries if the full result list does not fit in the visible recipe-book panel.
Recipe-book button positions can shift with GUI scale and window size. The plan identifies controls by their icon, label, tooltip, and resulting state rather than relying on fixed screen coordinates.

source_meta._title: The 'Hat' layer of a player skin is not shown in the tab list under certain conditions

stor.recommended_version: Minecraft Java Edition 1.21.1, the most recent release explicitly listed as affected in the report
stor.environment: Two authenticated Minecraft Java Edition clients using distinct player accounts and running exactly version 1.21.1. Use a LAN world hosted by the viewer client. The viewer remains in Creative mode and has permission to run commands; the target player is changed to Spectator mode. The target account must use a skin with a clearly visible, nontransparent outer head/hat layer.
preconditions: Label the two clients VIEWER and TARGET. VIEWER is the client from which the player list will be inspected; TARGET is the player whose head icon is being tested.
Both clients must run Minecraft Java Edition 1.21.1. Do not mix client or server versions.
VIEWER and TARGET must be logged in with different authenticated player accounts and therefore have different player names.

TARGET must have an active skin with a conspicuous nontransparent outer head layer, such as hair, a hood, glasses, or another design extending over the face or head. A skin whose outer head layer is completely transparent is unsuitable for this reproduction.
TARGET's Skin Customization setting named Hat must be ON.
The VIEWER-hosted LAN world must allow commands so VIEWER can change TARGET's game mode.
VIEWER must remain in a non-Spectator game mode throughout the trigger. This plan keeps VIEWER in Creative mode.
Use the configured List Players control when instructed to press Tab. Tab is the default key unless the control has been rebound.

steps.action: Configure and launch both Minecraft Java Edition clients using the release 1.21.1 installation. Log VIEWER and TARGET in with their respective distinct accounts.
steps.success_cue: Both clients reach the Minecraft 1.21.1 title screen under different player accounts.

steps.action: On TARGET, open the skin-part settings and enable the outer head layer. From the title screen select Options, select Skin Customization, set Hat to ON, and return to the title screen. If already in a world, use Esc before following the same Options path.
steps.exact_input: Options -> Skin Customization -> Hat: ON -> Done
steps.success_cue: TARGET's Skin Customization screen shows Hat: ON.

steps.action: On VIEWER, create a new single-player world in Creative mode. No particular seed, world type, coordinates, or difficulty are required by the report.
steps.exact_input: Singleplayer -> Create New World -> Game Mode: Creative -> Create New World
steps.success_cue: VIEWER has spawned in the new world with the Creative-mode hotbar visible and normal movement responding.

steps.action: On VIEWER, open the pause menu and expose the world to the local network. Enable commands before starting the LAN session.
steps.exact_input: Esc -> Open to LAN -> Game Mode: Creative -> Allow Cheats: ON -> Start LAN World
steps.success_cue: VIEWER returns to the world and a chat message reports that the local game has been hosted, normally including a port number.

steps.action: On TARGET, open Multiplayer, wait for the LAN world to appear, select it, and join it. If LAN discovery is unavailable, use Direct Connection with VIEWER's local network address and the port printed when the LAN world was opened.
steps.exact_input: Multiplayer -> select VIEWER's LAN world -> Join Server
steps.success_cue: TARGET finishes loading into the same world, and VIEWER receives or can see evidence that TARGET joined. Both clients remain connected and movement responds normally.

steps.action: Move VIEWER and TARGET into the same open area and place them several blocks apart, close enough that VIEWER can plainly see TARGET's player model. Avoid walls or terrain blocking the view.
steps.exact_input: Use the movement controls, normally W/A/S/D and Space in Creative mode, to position the players within visible range.
steps.success_cue: TARGET's complete player model is visibly rendered on VIEWER's screen.

steps.action: From VIEWER's client, look directly at TARGET and verify only the setup prerequisite that TARGET's selected skin has a visible outer layer around the head. If it is not visible, stop and correct TARGET's skin or Hat setting before continuing.
steps.exact_input: Move the mouse to aim VIEWER's camera at TARGET's head.
steps.success_cue: TARGET's in-world player model visibly has a distinguishable outer head layer, confirming that the selected skin can exercise the reported condition.

steps.action: Leave VIEWER in Creative mode. Do not switch VIEWER to Spectator mode during the remaining steps.
steps.success_cue: VIEWER remains in Creative mode and can see the normal hotbar; VIEWER is not spectating an entity or flying through blocks as a spectator.

steps.action: On VIEWER, open the in-game chat so the game-mode command can be run with the LAN host's command permission.
steps.success_cue: The chat input field is open on VIEWER's client.

steps.action: Enter the game-mode command, replacing the placeholder with TARGET's exact player name, and press Enter. Include the leading slash because the command is being entered in in-game chat.
steps.success_cue: A command confirmation states that TARGET's game mode was set to Spectator, and TARGET's client can fly freely and pass through solid blocks.

steps.action: Wait only until the game-mode change is complete and both clients respond normally. Keep TARGET connected in Spectator mode, and do not move TARGET back to another game mode.
steps.success_cue: TARGET is still connected in Spectator mode, VIEWER is still connected in Creative mode, and both clients respond to movement or camera input without world-loading interruption.

steps.action: On VIEWER, press and continue holding the List Players control, which is Tab by default. Do not release it before handing control to the observation subsystem.
steps.success_cue: The multiplayer player-list overlay is open on VIEWER's screen and includes an entry for the still-connected TARGET player.

stor.handoff_condition: VIEWER is holding the player-list overlay open while VIEWER remains in Creative mode and TARGET remains connected in Spectator mode. TARGET's entry is present in the overlay; begin visual observation of that entry now without changing either player's game mode or releasing Tab.
uncertainties: The report does not provide player names, accounts, or a specific skin file. The executor must supply a TARGET account with a clearly identifiable nontransparent outer head layer.

The report provides two alternative trigger conditions: placing TARGET in Spectator mode or moving TARGET far enough away that the player entity is no longer rendered. This plan selects the Spectator-mode variant because it is the simpler deterministic path and does not require estimating render distance.

The report permits either a multiplayer server or a LAN server. This plan selects a LAN world so VIEWER can deterministically obtain command permission without requiring separate dedicated-server configuration.
The exact wording of the LAN command-permission toggle can vary slightly by client UI; use the option that enables cheats or commands for the hosted LAN world.
Tab is the default List Players key, but the configured List Players control must be used if the key binding has been changed.
